name: Colorado

windshield.strip: nontransparent material may extend no more than four inches down from the top of the windshield; not red or amber; no glare reflection; windshield otherwise at least 70% light transmittance
windshield.reflective: material must not reflect sunlight or headlight glare more than the windshield without it

frontSide.note: any window except windshield: at least 27% light transmittance

backSide.note: may go below 27% if the front side windows and windshield allow at least 70%

rear.note: may go below 27% if front side windows and windshield allow at least 70%

tint.measuredHow: not stated (statute speaks of the window allowing 27% light transmittance)

reflectivity.front: no metallic or mirrored appearance on any window
reflectivity.back: no metallic or mirrored appearance on any window

medicalExemption.text: No medical exemption in C.R.S. § 42-4-227 as read (only law enforcement vehicles and factory federal-compliant glass)

penalty.text: Driving with non-compliant windows: class B traffic infraction ($15-$100); installing/treating a window that does not meet (1)(a): class A traffic infraction ($15-$100)

quotes: § 42-4-227(1)(a)(I): "...in such a way that it allows less than twenty-seven percent light transmittance. The windshield shall allow at least seventy percent light transmittance."

(1)(a)(II): "...the windows to the rear of the driver, including the rear window, may allow less than twenty-seven percent light transmittance if the front side windows and the windshield on such vehicles allow at least seventy percent light transmittance."
(1)(b)(I): "The bottom edge of the material extends no more than four inches measured from the top of the windshield down"
(1)(d): "No material shall be used on any window in the motor vehicle that presents a metallic or mirrored appearance."
(3)(a): "...any person who violates any provision of this section commits a class B traffic infraction."

helmet.conditions: Each person under 18 (driver or passenger) on a motorcycle, autocycle or low-power scooter must wear a DOT FMVSS 218 helmet

handheldPhone.noviceOrAgeBan: Drivers under 18 may not use a phone at all, including hands-free (CDOT)
handheldPhone.fineText: $75 fine and 2 points first offense; higher for repeat offenses; first offense dismissed with proof of purchase of a hands-free accessory (CDOT)
handheldPhone.cite: C.R.S. § 42-4-239 as amended by SB24-065 (effective Jan 1, 2025)

studdedTires.note: single-tired passenger vehicles and vehicles up to 3/4 ton: studs may not project more than 1/16 inch beyond the tread; no season in statute

radarDetector.note: No Colorado ban found; commercial vehicles over 10,001 lb banned federally (49 CFR 392.71)

openQuestions: leg.colorado.gov / content.leg.colorado.gov PDFs blocked by AWS WAF; statute text read on colorado.public.law, which reproduces the 2024 C.R.S. PDF - 2025/2026 amendments to 42-4-227 not verified
Medical exemption: none in statute as read; not confirmed against a CSP/DOR page

Hands-free law: CDOT says officer must witness careless/imprudent driving while holding the device, so treated as not purely primary; exact repeat-offense fines ($150 / $250 reported) not confirmed on an official page
Underglow and lift height: no specific Colorado rule found
